**Review of the October tins email**

Claim by claim:

- "Your subscription box left Bristol this morning." Fine. The brand is Bristol-based and tins are packed there. It's an operational statement, not a policy-listed claim, and nothing in it is contradicted.
- "a smoky lapsang and a soft white peony." Product description, fine.
- "you can pause or cancel any time from your account." This matches the approved claim "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time." Fine.
- Subject line "Your October tins are on the way" matches the content. Note that today is 17 November, so an "October" shipment is odd timing. Worth confirming the month is right, but I can't verify it, so it's a note and not a blocker.
- "Elevate your mornings:" is on the brand's banned word list ("elevate"). It's also generic marketing filler against the warm, plain, unhurried voice. This must change. A plain fix: "Something for your mornings:" or just drop it and go straight to "This month it's a smoky lapsang and a soft white peony."

No health, green, superlative, guarantee, urgency or testimonial issues. No disclosure label is needed, as this is the brand's own email. Spelling is UK-consistent.

Verdict: hold until "Elevate" is replaced, and confirm the month.
